correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the main objects and quantifiers of the target statement: a morphism f:P^N→P^N of degree d≥2 defined over a number field K, a positive constant C(f) depending on f, algebraic points P∈P^N(Q̄), the hypothesis that P is wandering for f, and a lower bound involving the canonical height and the extension degree [K(P):K]. These are exactly the ingredients of Conjecture 16.2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

refined_question: Let K be a number field, let f:P^N→P^N be a morphism of degree d≥2 defined over K, and for P∈P^N(Q̄) define the dynamical canonical height by ĥ_f(P)=lim_{n→∞} d^{-n}h(f^n(P)). If P=[a_0:…:a_N] and a_i≠0, let K(P)=K(a_0/a_i,…,a_N/a_i), and call P wandering if its forward orbit O_f(P)={f^n(P):n≥0} is infinite. Must there exist a constant C(f)>0, depending only on f, such that every wandering point P∈P^N(Q̄) satisfies ĥ_f(P) ≥ C(f)/[K(P):K]? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation your draft actually states is Conjecture 16.2. Its opening sentence is essentially Conjecture 16.2 verbatim, while the remainder of the draft switches into the paper’s transition paragraph introducing moduli height in order to state the different next conjecture, Conjecture 16.3. Because your draft never reaches the actual statement of Conjecture 16.3, the paper-faithful target is the Dynamical Lehmer Conjecture. The relevant surrounding context is Definition 16.1 for ĥ_f, equation (16.4) showing that this conjecture is a quantitative converse to vanishing of canonical height at preperiodic points, Definition 2.1 for “wandering,” and Section 3 for K(P). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
